searchText: from etherscan's perspective we'll want to index and have a dedicated label and dedicated page for displaying withdrawals on the execution layer - a special txtype is ideal for us - alternatively, it could be done as part of an 'internal transaction' and sent from a specific contract - eip 4895 operations work too as long as the withdrawals are returned via RPC calls but as long as there is a clear indication we'll be good - will do everything we can to support wondering if there's inspiration to be found in how bridges handle cross-chain details with their balance transfers If it is a special system transaction then most likely it would be a new array of things on the block. When processing a block, you would iterate over that array and process them as appropriate (in this case updating recipient balances and whatnot). This list would, presumably, be returned when you query for the block via JSON-RPC. Yeah, it might be interesting to see if L2 solutions would have a preference either way and could adopt the same mechansim. EIP-4844 now has a "meta spec", an aggregate of all the different resources: https://hackmd.io/@protolambda/eip4844-meta Eventually I hope the technical execution-layer contents can move to the execution-specs, and the EIP itself can be more of a resource linking all involved specs (API, EL specs, CL specs, KZG ceremony, etc.) together with a human readable summary. <@!552133098075193354> I'm looking forward to your proposal for cross-layer EIPs next ACD call. On my TODO to draft it, after Kiln stuff is wrapped up 🙂

excerpts.author: harithk
excerpts.content:
from etherscan's perspective we'll want to index and have a dedicated label and dedicated page for displaying withdrawals on the execution layer

- a special txtype is ideal for us
- alternatively, it could be done as part of an 'internal transaction' and sent from a specific contract
- eip 4895 operations work too as long as the withdrawals are returned via RPC calls

but as long as there is a clear indication we'll be good - will do everything we can to support
